_comment: Per-query expectations for --data (production) mode. Fixture mode still compares .expected exactly and still fails on zero rows. A query with NO entry here fails in production mode: that keeps 'empty is a failure' the default and makes every exemption a visible edit. An exemption is may_be_empty with a reason, never a min_rows of 0 -- the distinction between 'this export has none' and 'we stopped checking' is the whole point.

cq01-market-proposition.why: Requires wx:atSite and the climatological day's boundary instants, both of which an export omits by design. cq01 is a fixture-mode question: it describes a market fully, and a full description is not what an export carries. cq02 and cq04 are the production floors.

cq02-probability-gap.why: The forecast side and the market side must both point at at least one shared proposition. Empty means the join broke, which is the failure this phase exists to catch.

cq04-settlement-provenance.why: The export is built for a day that has a daily_settlements row, so a settlement chain is always expected. Empty means the chain did not serialize.

cq05-bracket-coherence.why: Needs a grouping asserted mutually exclusive. An export carrying one market of a ladder has no grouping to check, and exporting the whole ladder is not required.

cq06a-calibration-reliability.why: Calibration needs scored history across many days. A single-day export has one assignment at most, and omits the model runs cq06 groups by.

cq06b-skill-by-leadtime.why: Same as cq06a: skill by lead time needs a model run and a history, both of which the export omits by design.

cq07-correction-contradiction.why: Only populated when the settlement source issued a correction. Most days have none, and a day that has one is the interesting case, not the required one.

cq08-order-flow-payout.why: The export omits the trading layer entirely -- no orders, trades, lots or payouts. Empty here is the export being what it says it is.
